text: Comic Sans 最可怕的地方是，它不是难看，它是“过于热情”。每个字母都像刚从幼儿园手工课跑出来，歪着头问你：“我可爱吗？”你看那个大写 C，像没画完的月亮；那个 S，扭得像在逃避责任。它本来是给漫画对话框用的，结果有人拿它写简历、讣告、公司通知。Comic Sans 一出现，内容立刻从“严肃声明”变成“老师我忘带作业了”。
PHP最像一个情绪不稳定的会计：每个变量前都要先交一块钱，$name、$age，连穷都穷得很规范。它的“==”更吓人，"0e123"能等于"0e456"，黑客看了都想考会计证。最崩溃是strpos，找到在第0位，它返回0；你一判断if，它说没找到。PHP：我不是bug，我是考验你对“存在”的哲学理解。
Papyrus 这个字体最神奇的地方，是它明明出生在电脑里，却一脸“我刚从埃及墓里拓出来”的样子。每个字母边缘都像被耗子啃过，还特别自信：A 像叉开腿的木乃伊，R 像法老写到一半抽筋。你用它打“Wi-Fi 密码”，瞬间像古代诅咒；打“今日特价披萨”，就像出土文物旁边贴了二维码。最离谱是《阿凡达》也用它，外星文明飞船都有了，审美还停在 Windows 字体库第一层。

PHP is what happens when a templating language finds a server, moves in, and refuses to leave. Every variable starts with a dollar sign because even the syntax knows you’ll pay for this later. Its idea of equality is “sure, close enough,” so `"0" == false` like it’s doing improv with your authentication. The standard library was apparently named during a hostage situation: `strpos($haystack, $needle)` here, `array_search($needle, $haystack)` there—consistency is for languages with self-esteem. It gave us `mysql_query`, magic quotes, register globals, and then acted shocked when the internet caught fire. PHP arrays are lists, maps, stacks, queues, and emotional support objects. And namespaces use backslashes, because forward slashes were too readable.

Comic Sans is what happens when a font puts on Crocs and calls it “business casual.” Designed for comic speech bubbles, somehow it escaped into school newsletters, passive-aggressive office signs, and funeral programs that look like they were catered by a daycare. Every letter looks like it was hand-drawn by a substitute teacher during indoor recess. The “S” has the posture of a pool noodle, the “M” looks like it’s apologizing, and the kerning feels supervised by a sugar-high toddler. Comic Sans doesn’t say “friendly”; it says “I printed this from Windows 95 and didn’t know fonts were optional.” It’s the only typeface that can make a warning sign look like it’s asking nicely before the forklift hits you.

Papyrus is what happens when a font goes on one mission trip to Egypt and never stops talking about it. Every letter looks like it was carved into a damp napkin by a youth pastor opening a smoothie bar. It has the confidence of hieroglyphics and the authenticity of a mall kiosk selling “ancient” bracelets next to phone cases. Designers see Papyrus and immediately start hearing pan flutes in a dentist’s waiting room. It’s the official typeface of vegan cafés, church retreat flyers, and restaurants named “Nile Breeze” that serve microwaved falafel. Even the rough edges feel fake, like it bought distressing pre-ripped from Urban Outfitters. Papyrus doesn’t say “timeless.” It says, “I found the text tool in 2003 and chose culture.”

JavaScript is the only language where “0 == false” is true, “0 == []” is true, but somehow “[] == false” is also true, like it learned logic from a group chat. It has `NaN`, which stands for “Not a Number,” and naturally `typeof NaN` is `"number"`—because gaslighting is a core feature.  

The language looked at classes and said, “What if we made them fake, but confidently?” Then it gave us `this`, a keyword so unstable it needs therapy and a binding strategy. JavaScript runs everywhere: browsers, servers, fridges—because apparently one runtime escaping containment wasn’t enough. And npm? A beautiful ecosystem where your production app depends on 900 packages, three of which pad strings and one of which is maintained by a raccoon.

JavaScript最像前任：你以为你了解它，它说“[] + []等于空字符串”，你忍了；“[] + {}等于[object Object]”，你也忍；“{} + []等于0”，你开始怀疑人生。最绝的是NaN，名字叫“不是数字”，但typeof NaN是number。null更狠，typeof null是object——这语言连“空”都要假装有房。写到最后，bug不是我写的，是JS自己“自动类型转换”感情用事。

Papyrus. The official font of a 43-year-old white woman opening a holistic crystal healing shop in a strip mall. You look like somebody wrote the alphabet with a frayed stick dipped in herbal tea. You’re not ancient Egyptian, Papyrus, you’re the default choice for a mid-tier Mediterranean restaurant that definitely microwaves its falafel. 

It is truly amazing how one typeface can simultaneously scream "youth group retreat" and "James Cameron’s multi-billion dollar sci-fi epic." The director of *Avatar* really looked at a drop-down menu on Microsoft Word 2003 and said, "Yes, this perfectly captures the majesty of giant blue aliens." 

You are the Comic Sans of the spiritual community. If a flyer has Papyrus on it, there is a one hundred percent chance it smells like patchouli and is inviting me to an unmedicated birth.

Let's talk about Comic Sans. The only font that walks onto a printed resume and says, "I brought juice boxes!" It is the typographic equivalent of a grown adult wearing a propeller beanie to a funeral. Why do people keep using this for serious announcements? You can’t put an eviction notice in Comic Sans. "You have thirty days to vacate"—oh, fun, are there going to be clowns? It was literally designed for a 1990s Microsoft cartoon dog, and somehow it became the official typeface of passive-aggressive office breakroom signs. No, Brenda, your threat to throw away my Tupperware isn't intimidating when it looks like it was written by a toddler fist-gripping a cheap crayon. Comic Sans is the only font in the dropdown menu that makes Papyrus look like a respectable life choice.

你们见过Comic Sans吗？这绝对是字体界的“小丑套装”。它明明是微软给卡通狗说话设计的，偏偏有人觉得它“很亲切”，到处乱用。

我昨天拿到一份体检报告，医生居然用了Comic Sans！就那种圆滚滚、像小学生用蜡笔涂出来的字母，上面写着：“你可能有个恶性肿瘤。”

看着这行字，我根本没法害怕。我只觉得我的肿瘤下一秒就要配着“Boing”的卡通音效跳出来说：“Ta-da！惊不惊喜？”

这字体太滑稽了。你用它写辞职信，老板都不会生气，他只会觉得你明天要回幼儿园当大班班长了。

PHP is the only language that demands a dollar sign before every single variable, yet pays its developers the least. It’s a language designed by a guy who clearly hated consistency. How do you manipulate a string? Is it `strpos`? `str_replace`? Do the arguments go needle-haystack or haystack-needle? Nobody knows! You just guess and refresh the browser.

And let's talk about error messages. In what other universe do you miss a colon and get screamed at by an ancient Hebrew demon? *Parse error: unexpected T_PAAMAYIM_NEKUDOTAYIM.* Bless you? No, curse you. 

People keep saying PHP is dead, but it’s really just the cockroach of the web. You try to kill it, but then you realize half the internet is held together by a WordPress plugin written in 2008 by a teenager who thought `include_once("header.php")` was peak software architecture.

你们知道吗，Comic Sans 根本不是一个字体，它是一封来自1994年的求救信。每次看到它，我都觉得这字不是写出来的，是逃出来的。就像幼儿园老师画完太阳后顺手把字也画了。最气人的是它还很自信，你知道吧？那种“嗨！我在一张严肃的通知上！惊喜吗？”的表情。你要是在简历上用它，HR看完会觉得自己的人生被贴了张便利贴，上面写着“随便吧”。其实我挺想跟发明它的人聊聊，真的，我想问他：你是不是打赌输了？赌注是“设计一个让所有文字都像在道歉的字体”？

Comic Sans, you are the typographic equivalent of a middle-aged dad wearing a backwards cap and saying “How do you do, fellow kids?” You were *designed* by a Microsoft employee looking at a comic book and thinking, “What if the font itself had a learning disability?” You’re not casual, you’re a cry for help.

You show up to every passive-aggressive office kitchen note like, “Your mother doesn’t work here, Karen.” You’re the font of choice for church bulletins, lemonade stands run by convicted felons, and dentists who still have magazines from 2007. You make a funeral program look like a child’s birthday invitation. You’ve ruined more résumés than a criminal record.

Every time a graphic designer sees you on a business card, a puppy gets kicked. You’re not a font; you’re the typographical version of a participation trophy that somehow got promoted to assistant manager. And the worst part? You *know* you’re bad, and you still show up to work every day, grinning like an idiot.

你们见过Papyrus这个字体吗？就是那个边缘坑坑洼洼、自带风化效果，像是一个手抖的古埃及法老在枯树皮上硬挠出来的字。

只要一家店用它做招牌，你闭着眼都能猜到，里面要么卖死海泥手工皂，要么做脉轮精油推拿。它身上有种极其廉价的异域神秘学气质。

这也是我至今无法原谅《阿凡达》的原因。卡梅隆砸了三亿美金搞外星特效，电影Logo却像他午休时在Word下拉菜单里随手选的。看着屏幕上那串破破烂烂的Papyrus，我根本不相信外星人在拯救潘多拉星，我觉得他下一秒就要给我推销塔罗牌占卜。

Papyrus字体，你是从古埃及壁画上直接扒下来的吗？每次看到它，我都觉得下一句应该是“本店招牌：木乃伊烤串”。为什么一个字体能同时做到又古朴又廉价？它就像个穿草裙的会计，原始和严谨两头都不沾。用它写“生日快乐”，看起来像法老在诅咒你；用它写“禁止停车”，我觉得下面该画个圣甲虫。更绝的是，这个字体还自带一股霉味，好像刚从金字塔里挖出来，隔着屏幕都能闻见三千年的灰。设计师选它的时候是不是刚看完《木乃伊归来》？

很多人喊“PHP是世界上最好的语言”，但我一上手就崩溃了。

这语言太财迷了吧！每个变量前面非得加个美元符号“$”。你写个$wife，写个$car，敲代码时感觉自己像个土豪，结果一看工资条，还没隔壁写Java的零头多。

而且它调对象属性特别繁琐。别的语言打个点“.”就行，PHP非要画个箭头“->”，你得连按减号和大于号。

我觉得写PHP根本不是在面向对象编程，完全是交通协管员在路口指挥交通：“那个变量，往前走！这个对象，右拐！”

You’re the font equivalent of a middle-aged man wearing a puka shell necklace and calling himself “shaman.” Your rough, distressed edges aren’t rustic—they’re just badly drawn, like a toddler tried to carve letters into a wet napkin. You’re the typographic version of a “Live, Laugh, Love” sign in a suburban bathroom. Every time a graphic designer sees you, they don’t think “ancient wisdom”—they think “unpaid intern with a pirated copy of Photoshop.” You’re the official font of mediocre Thai restaurants, low-budget fantasy novels, and James Cameron’s worst creative decision since “unobtanium.” You’re not timeless, Papyrus. You’re a cry for help in faux-Egyptian cosplay. Even Comic Sans gets invited to ironic parties. You just get left off the guest list.

JavaScript, you’re the only language that treats logic like a casual suggestion. You were thrown together in ten days back in 1995, and buddy, we are all still paying the price. 

Let’s talk about your math. Why does an array plus an array equal an empty string, but an array plus an object is `[object Object]`? And `typeof NaN` returns "number"? That’s like saying the type of virgin is "parent."

Your equality checks are just pure gaslighting. `0 == "0"` is true. `0 == []` is true. So `"0" == []` must be true, right? Nope, false! 

And nobody actually knows what `this` is. We just keep guessing contexts until the console stops screaming. You’re the only ecosystem where downloading a simple text formatting package gives you a `node_modules` folder heavier than a dying star.

PHP is what happens when a language is designed by a committee of people who each had a different favorite other language, and they all agreed to compromise by making it worse. You've got `strpos` and `str_rot13`, because one day someone said, "You know what would be fun? Random underscores." Needle, haystack? Haystack, needle? PHP flips a coin on every function. And the type juggling—comparing `"1e3"` to `"1000"` gives true, because PHP thinks numbers are just vibes. Error handling? Half the functions return `false`, the other half throw warnings you're supposed to ignore. And let's not forget: the original creator built it in his spare time to track traffic to his homepage. It shows. PHP is a language that peaked at WordPress security patches and never looked back. It's not a scripting language; it's a hostage situation.

JavaScript is the only language where `NaN === NaN` is false, yet somehow `[] + []` is an empty string, and `[] + {}` is "[object Object]". It’s like a toddler with a chemistry set: no idea what it’s doing, but it’s very confident. You wanted a programming language; you got a chaos engine that thinks `"10" - 1` is 9, but `"10" + 1` is "101"—because math is hard when your brain runs on memes. And the ecosystem? Ten thousand dependencies to left-pad a string. You don’t debug JavaScript; you negotiate with it. It’s not a language, it’s a hostage situation with semicolons that are optional except when they ruin your entire Tuesday.

你们知道PHP的数组吧？它既是数组又是字典，还是队列，偶尔客串一下栈。你永远不知道下一秒它想扮演什么角色。还有那个`==`和`===`，PHP说：“两个字符串‘123’和整数123，我觉得它们差不多。”你写代码的时候以为自己在做比较，其实是在做性格测试。最绝的是命名，`strpos`、`str_rot13`、`nl2br`，没有规律，像考英语四六级时瞎蒙的完形填空。每一次写PHP，都像在跟一个喝醉的翻译官交流——你说A，它给你回个“差不多先生”。

JavaScript最伟大的发明就是`==`，它让数学老师集体失业。你随便写`0 == "0"`，它说true；`0 == []`，它也true；`0 == "\t"`，还是true。更离谱的是`[] == ![]`，左边是空数组，右边是“非空数组”，它俩居然相等。你说那行，我用`===`总行了吧？结果`NaN === NaN`是false，唯一的数字跟它自己都不相等。这哪是语言啊，这是薛定谔的布尔值——你不打开控制台，永远不知道它是不是在逗你。

JavaScript就像个喜欢PUA你的渣男。你问它：“数字1加字符串1等于几？”它说：“11。”你想，行，加号代表字符串拼接。你又问：“那字符串1减去1呢？”它说：“等于0。”怎么着？遇见加号你是文学家，遇见减号你就突然想起自己是个计算器了？

最离谱的是，你问它：“Not a Number，也就是NaN，到底属于什么类型？”它笃定地说：“它是一个Number。”你听听这是人话吗？“不是数字”的类型居然是数字！这就好比你指着包装上的“无骨鸡爪”问老板这到底是个啥，老板理直气壮地说：“它是一根骨头。”

Papyrus, the font that says, “I watched Avatar in a parking lot and now I run a yoga studio.” You’re not ancient, you’re a default preset with a thirst for authenticity. Your little fibrous curls look like a scroll got nervous in a printer queue. Every artisan soap label, every discount mystic, every “Grand Opening” banner borrows you because they think elegance means looking mildly water-damaged. You’re the typeface equivalent of a clay pendant: earthy, dated, and convinced you have meaning. Even Comic Sans gets laughed with; you get laminated at a strip-mall tarot shop and called sacred.

Comic Sans, you’re the typographic equivalent of a clown honking at a funeral. You show up to school newsletters, lemonade stands, and passive-aggressive office signs like nobody asked for your wobbly little letterforms. Your “a” looks like it gave up halfway through being a letter, and your lowercase “g” is just a pretzel having a panic attack. You were built for cartoon speech bubbles, yet somehow became the font choice for people who think kerning is a type of yoga. Doctors use you for medical warnings, and suddenly the prognosis feels like a lost birthday invitation. Even Times New Roman—a font that smells like photocopier dust—looks at you and whispers, “Have some self-respect.”

PHP is the programming equivalent of a 1998 minivan with a jet engine duct-taped to the roof: it’ll get you there, but everyone hears you coming and nobody trusts the brakes. It’s a language where function names are an inconsistent lottery, strings and numbers flirt until runtime confesses, and the manual somehow reads like sacred scripture and IKEA instructions. WordPress runs half the web, which mostly proves the web has a survival instinct, not taste. Laravel shows up in a tuxedo to apologize for PHP’s bare feet, while every legacy codebase hides a mysql_connect call like a cursed family heirloom. Even the mascot is an elephant, because PHP never forgets what it did to your type safety.

Comic Sans has a number of practical strengths. Its rounded, open letterforms are highly legible at small sizes and are often considered easier to read for some individuals with dyslexia. The typeface conveys a warm, approachable tone that works well in informal materials, children’s resources, and casual communications. However, these same qualities limit its appropriateness. Its playful appearance can undermine credibility in formal, corporate, or serious documents, and its widespread use has made it feel visually tired to many readers. From a design standpoint, the font lacks refined spacing and consistent weight distribution, which can create a slightly uneven texture in longer passages. Comic Sans is not inherently poor, but it succeeds only when its friendly character matches the context and audience.

Comic Sans 字体由微软设计师 Vincent Connare 于1994年创作，灵感来自漫画书对话气泡中的手写字体。它的优点是亲切、非正式，易读性较高，对儿童和有阅读障碍的人群有一定友好度。在幼儿园通知、生日邀请、非正式演示等轻松场合，它能营造温和、随意的氛围。

不足之处在于，它常被误用于正式商业文档、严肃公告或公共标识等场合，显得不够庄重，字形细节和排版专业感也弱于经典正文字体。长期过度使用使其在专业设计领域口碑不佳。总体而言，Comic Sans 并非没有价值，关键在于场合是否匹配，轻松、教育或儿童相关场景中可发挥亲和力，但不适合传达权威或正式信息。

我最怕公司用 Comic Sans 发裁员通知。那字体本身就像每个字母都穿着彩色袜子：a 圆得像刚学会站稳，S 扭得像幼儿园滑梯，逗号像融化的小糖豆。你点开一封“业务调整公告”，标题却是 Comic Sans，感觉下一秒不是“很遗憾”，而是“小朋友，今天没有饼干了”。它不是普通难看，是气质失控：墓碑上刻 Comic Sans，像逝者最后一句话是“嘿嘿”。设计师看见它不是皱眉，是想报警，像有人把蜡笔扔进他的黑咖啡。别的字体是在说话，Comic Sans 是举手问：老师，我可爱吗？

Papyrus 字体具有鲜明的手写与仿古特征，边缘略带不规则，给人一种温暖、自然、质朴的感觉。它在标题、邀请函、手工艺或与自然、历史相关的设计中有一定表现力，容易营造轻松、亲切的氛围，辨识度也比较高。

不足方面，Papyrus 的字重和样式选择较少，排版灵活性有限；正文中使用时清晰度和易读性不够理想。由于过去被广泛使用，它容易显得缺乏新意，在正式、专业或现代感较强的场合中不太合适。总体而言，这是一款个性突出但适用范围较窄的字体，需要谨慎选择使用场景。

Papyrus is a distinctive typeface with a handcrafted, organic quality. Its rough edges and irregular letterforms evoke a sense of antiquity and warmth, which can work well for themed packaging, invitations, or artistic projects seeking a natural, earthy feel. However, the typeface has notable limitations. Its textured strokes and uneven spacing reduce legibility at small sizes and in dense text, making it unsuitable for body copy or formal documents. Additionally, its widespread use in inappropriate contexts has made it feel clichéd to many viewers, and the lack of a true bold or italic variant limits typographic flexibility. Overall, Papyrus can be effective when used sparingly and in the right setting, but it is rarely a safe choice for professional or neutral communication.

PHP是一门在Web开发领域有着深厚积累的语言，上手门槛低，部署非常方便，几乎所有主流主机环境都能直接运行。它的生态成熟，拥有WordPress、Laravel、Symfony等大量框架和内容管理系统，适合快速构建网站与中小型应用。PHP 7之后的性能提升明显，执行效率已经能满足多数业务场景。

不足之处也比较明显。语言早期设计存在不一致之处，函数命名和参数顺序不够统一，给学习和维护带来一些困扰。类型系统虽然持续改进，但历史遗留的宽松行为仍可能导致隐蔽问题。此外，在高并发、长连接和异步处理方面，它的原生能力相对一些现代语言还有差距。

总体而言，PHP务实、高效且生态丰富，尤其在传统Web项目中依然是非常可靠的选择。

PHP remains a practical and widely supported language for web development. Its strengths include straightforward deployment on most shared hosts, a large ecosystem of frameworks and libraries, extensive documentation, and meaningful performance and type-safety improvements in recent releases. For many small to medium projects, PHP allows rapid development with minimal configuration.

At the same time, the language carries some notable weaknesses. Its standard library has historical inconsistencies in function naming and argument order, which can make the API harder to learn and remember. Older codebases and tutorials often reflect outdated practices, and the language’s permissiveness can enable security mistakes if developers are not careful. While modern PHP has addressed many earlier criticisms, its reputation and legacy quirks still require careful attention. Overall, PHP is a capable tool whose effectiveness depends on disciplined use and current best practices.

我最怕JavaScript，它不是语言，是案发现场。你问typeof null，它说是object；你问NaN === NaN，它说false，连自己都认不出自己。加号一来更离谱：[] + {}是字符串，{} + []能变0，数学老师看完想报警。写this才叫刺激，普通函数一套，回调一套，箭头函数又一套，this永远指向你心理防线崩溃的方向。最离谱是sort()，10能排在2前面，因为人家按字符串排。面试官还问为什么0.1 + 0.2 !== 0.3？我说因为JavaScript把精确当建议。

JavaScript is a widely supported language that runs in every major browser, making it essential for web development. Its event-driven model and asynchronous capabilities allow responsive applications, and the ecosystem offers many libraries and tools. However, the language has some inconsistencies in type coercion and comparison behavior, which can lead to subtle bugs if not carefully managed. The rapid pace of framework changes can also make long-term maintenance challenging, and performance can vary across environments. Overall, JavaScript is a capable and flexible tool, but developers benefit from a solid understanding of its quirks and disciplined coding practices.

JavaScript 是一种应用广泛的编程语言。它的优点较为明显：在浏览器中具有原生支持，几乎无需额外环境即可运行；事件驱动和异步模型适合处理交互与网络请求；借助 Node.js 还可用于服务端开发，前后端技术栈相对统一，生态和社区资源也很丰富。不足之处同样值得注意：动态类型和隐式类型转换容易使错误在运行时才暴露，增加调试成本；部分历史遗留的语法和行为不够一致，会给初学者带来困惑；复杂场景下回调与异步流程的可读性会下降，性能也不如一些静态编译语言。总体而言，它实用、灵活，但在工程化应用中往往需要借助规范和工具来弥补自身不足。

JavaScript is the language where [] + {} is "[object Object]", {} + [] is 0, and NaN !== NaN because even math needs gaslighting. It ships undefined as a function, typeof null as "object", and a package manager where left-pad can collapse civilization. You can write async code that still feels synchronous only if you remember to await every promise, or one typo becomes an unhandled rejection. It has this that changes based on vibes, prototypes pretending not to be classes, and equality so flexible that "0" == false but "0" !== false. JavaScript: the only ecosystem where you install 4,000 modules to center a div, then complain about bundle size in a language that can't agree whether 1 plus "1" is 2 or "11".

Typefaces are the participation trophies of design. Every one of them is just the same alphabet with a personality crisis—some are the guy at the party who won't stop talking about kerning; others are the beige wallpaper of every office memo ever printed. You had one job: make letters look like letters, and somehow you've convinced the world you're art. Congratulations, you're just handwriting that went to private school. You've got a thousand weights, but none of them carry any actual meaning. The bold ones are passive-aggressive underlines waiting to happen; the light ones vanish if you squint. And don't get me started on italics—leaning slightly to the right is not a personality. You're the garnish on a sentence, the spray tan on the alphabet. Nobody reads a love letter and says, "Wow, that ampersand really sold it." You're all just vowels in varying states of undress.

Web programming languages are the only tools where “it works on my machine” is considered a deployment strategy. You people treat dependencies like Pokémon—gotta collect ’em all—until your node_modules folder weighs more than your actual application and your build pipeline needs its own support group. Every six months there’s a new framework that solves the problems created by the last framework, which was supposed to solve the problems from the one before that. You’re not engineers; you’re archaeologists digging through layers of abandoned syntax. And the best part? None of you agree on anything. Ask ten web devs how to center a div and you’ll get eleven opinions, a Medium article, and a guy who insists you should just use tables like it’s 1999. Your entire ecosystem is a Rube Goldberg machine made of left-pad and regret.

你们有没有想过，Web编程语言就像相亲市场上的简历，每个都吹自己“简单”“强大”“全能”，结果你一上手，发现它们连“你好，世界”都得先让你配个环境。  
那些语言天天更新，版本号比我的体重涨得还快，今天说“我们全面支持模块化”，明天又喊“我们拥抱异步并发”，后天又哭“其实我们想变回简单”。你刚学会写个按钮，它们已经进化到能自动帮你修水龙头了。  
最气人的是，所有教程第一句都是：“先打开终端。”我要是会终端，我还学你？我直接黑进银行不好吗？

Web programming languages are the only tools where “it works on my machine” is considered a personality trait. They’re a support group for people who enjoy explaining why their framework isn’t just a library, but actually a config file with extra steps. You burn four hours configuring a build tool to print “Hello World,” then call yourself an engineer. The whole ecosystem is a circle jerk of devs rewriting the same to-do app in a slightly different syntax, then blogging about how the old way was garbage. They’re less programming languages and more elaborate machines for turning coffee into stack traces. You don’t write code—you assemble dependencies until the error messages start feeling like old friends. And the best part? A browser update will break everything by Tuesday. It’s not software development, it’s a hostage negotiation with the DOM.

Typefaces, you're all just letters with a publicist. Every one of you claims to have a "personality"—you're ink on a screen, not a person. You're the tofu of design: no flavor, just whatever shape the page needs. You have more weights than a gym of insecure teenagers, yet you can't carry a sentence without kerning therapy. You're all variations of circles and sticks that got together and agreed to act important because someone once gave you a name. "Timeless"? You're not timeless, you're just a letter that couldn't commit to being a circle or a rectangle, so you became both and called it design. The only thing you've revolutionized is how people argue about boring documents. Get over yourselves. You're not a voice; you're a wardrobe for vowels.

我最怕Papyrus。别的字体排版，它招魂。它每个字母都像被砂纸打磨过，边缘毛得像刚从尼罗河捞出来的莎草纸。大写A像金字塔塌了一角，小写y像晒干的芦苇杆，s拐弯像象形文字没刻完就下班。它一出现，再正经的内容都像足疗店菜单或小学历史手抄报。最离谱的是它自带“我很古老我很贵”的气质，可现实里永远配着“开业酬宾，足疗六十八”。有人用Papyrus做PPT，我感觉下一页不是季度数据，是法老诅咒：凡阅读此页者，加班至王朝覆灭。

我最近发现，现代人的身份焦虑全在字体上。你写个方案，内容还没想好，先打开字体列表，像选人生伴侣一样往下滑。这个太胖，那个太细，这个看着像刚离婚。最后选了一个“低调有内涵”的，发给领导，领导电脑没装，打开全变成默认。你所有的努力，在别人屏幕上就是四个字：系统自带。

还有那些艺术字体，设计出来就不是为了让你读，是为了让你猜。你盯着看半天，感觉每个字都在冲你抛媚眼，“猜猜我是谁呀？”我不是来认字的，我是来破案的。

最绝的是免费字体。好看的全要钱，免费的全是一种气质——凑合。用它做海报，客户问我，你们公司是不是快倒闭了？

我字已经够丑了，现在连打出来的字都透露着寒酸。

Web编程语言这一整个物种，都活得像时尚圈。今天流行这个，明天流行那个，你以为你在学技术，其实你在追季度新款。它们的共同点是：全都在说“我很简单”，结果你连环境都搭不起来。你写一行代码，它给你报三个错，每个错都指向另一个配置文件，配置文件里还有一行注释：“别问为什么，问就是历史原因。”我上次想写个网页，打开文档第一页写着“请先安装这十七个工具”，我装到第三个就放弃了。现在那个网页还显示着“正在加载中”，已经加载了两年。最绝的是，这些语言各有各的信仰，但每一个都坚称别的语言在浪费时间。我作为用户就想问一句：你们能不能选出一个，先把“按钮点击后变个颜色”这件事给我做顺了？就这么个需求，你们整得跟登陆火星似的。谢谢，我继续去更新依赖了。

字体就是文字的皮肤。同一句话换个字体，意思完全不同。你给喜欢的人发“在吗”，用正式字体像法院传票，用圆滚滚字体像撒娇。但对方根本不会注意，只会回你一个“嗯”，用的还是默认字体。

最烦选字体。写辞职信，选字体比写内容还紧张。太正式显得蓄谋已久，太随意显得不尊重公司，最后选了默认字体，老板一看：哦，这人已经崩溃了。其实你只是懒得往下翻。

字体名字也玄乎，都叫什么细的、黑的、圆的、简的，听着像奶茶店的新品，什么半糖、去冰、加脆波波。你喝一口发现还是白开水。你电脑里存了两百种字体，真正用的永远是默认那个。剩下那一百九十九种，存在的意义就是让你在选字体的时候，觉得自己很有品味。

朋友问我为什么还写PHP，我说它特别念旧。别的语言讲类型安全，PHP还用==搞人情世故：'0'==false成立，一上===就翻脸。变量必须带$，写代码像发红包：$name、$db，少一个就报未定义。函数名像拼图：strpos找位置，stripos忽略大小写，str_replace替换，记不住就查文档。最离谱是HTML里夹<?php echo ?>，像把服务器包进饺子。别人报错给堆栈，PHP直接提醒你headers already sent，就因为你多打一个回车，你说气不气人。

Jackfruit is what happens when a pineapple gets cursed by a durian and decides to dress like a medieval weapon. It’s the size of a toddler, covered in spikes, and somehow still has the confidence to smell like bubblegum left in a gym bag. People say it’s a miracle meat substitute, which is insulting to both miracles and meat. You spend forty minutes cutting it open, oiling your knife like you’re performing surgery on a haunted cactus, just to get sticky latex all over your hands and a pile of yellow pods that taste like mangoes with commitment issues. And the seeds? Great, a bonus chore. Jackfruit isn’t a fruit; it’s a hostile workplace with fiber.
榴莲这东西最邪门，外面长得像中世纪兵器，里面软得像投降书。你说它是水果吧，开它得像拆炸弹：先戴手套，再找裂口，最后全家后退三步。最离谱的是味道，没打开之前是邻居报警，打开之后是物业上门，吃完打个嗝，感觉嘴里有个小区垃圾站在开业。可它还贵，买的时候像买奢侈品，拎回家像携带危险品，吃两口还得说“真香”，不然显得自己很没见识。

Durian is the only fruit that shows up smelling like a gas leak and still has the confidence to charge premium prices. It looks like a medieval weapon, smells like onions lost a custody battle with gym socks, and somehow tastes like custard made in a haunted dumpster. People say, “You have to get past the smell.” Great pitch—same thing they say about sewage treatment plants. Hotels ban it like it’s a tiny green war criminal. Public transit sees a durian and says, “Absolutely not, we have standards,” which is bold for public transit. And durian fans are always so dramatic: “It’s the king of fruits!” Yeah, because it rules through fear, spikes, and chemical warfare.
拉斯维加斯最厉害的地方，是它把“沙漠里缺水”包装成景点。贝拉吉奥喷泉一放，旁边游客鼓掌：哇，好浪漫！我心想，这要在别的沙漠，叫浪费水资源；在Vegas，叫整点表演。威尼斯人更绝，沙漠里挖条运河，找人划贡多拉，还唱意大利歌。你以为自己在欧洲，其实你在内华达，被空调和度假村费联合绑架。连机场都有老虎机，欢迎你：行李可能晚点，但破产可以准点。
菠萝蜜这个水果很离谱，长得像榴莲的健身教练，一颗抱回家跟搬家一样。切开更刺激，刀刚碰上去就开始流白胶，像水果界的502，切完我手、刀、砧板全签了终身合同。它还不是给你一口一口吃的，得在一堆黄色小房间里找果肉，每瓣里面还藏一颗大籽，像买了精装房，实际得自己拆迁。最气的是，吃完满屋子都是味儿，不臭，但特别霸道：第二天朋友一进门，说你家昨天是不是来过一辆热带卡车？

Las Vegas is what happens when a strip mall wins the lottery and immediately develops a cocaine problem. It’s the only city where the airport has slot machines, because apparently losing money after landing was too subtle. The Strip is just Times Square in a bedazzled tank top, sweating under a fake Eiffel Tower while a guy dressed as Fat Elvis charges twenty bucks for a blurry photo. Vegas built canals in the desert, pyramids without history, and New York without rent control—then called it culture. Even the fountains at Bellagio look like they’re trying to distract you from your credit card statement. And Fremont Street? That’s where neon goes when it violates parole. Las Vegas: proof that if you add enough lights, people will call dehydration “a weekend getaway.”

Macau is what happens when Portugal, China, and a slot machine all lose a bet together. It’s so dense even the sidewalks need personal space. The skyline looks like a casino tycoon designed it during a fever dream, especially the Grand Lisboa, which screams, “What if a pineapple became a knife?” You’ve got UNESCO heritage sites wedged between baccarat tables like history got trapped in a shopping mall. The Ruins of St. Paul’s is literally just a façade, which is also the city’s whole personality after you lose your ferry money. And the egg tarts are incredible—because after three hours in Cotai, you need one thing in Macau that isn’t trying to bankrupt you.
澳门这个地方特别神奇，面积小到你导航还没说完“前方五十米”，你已经出境了。白天大家在大三巴前拍照，拍完发现背后就一堵墙，像景点也开了“轻资产模式”。晚上更离谱，整座城金光闪闪，全是赌场酒店，走进去以为自己是贵宾，出来才知道自己只是给威尼斯人的天花板赞助了一颗灯泡。澳门最狠的是蛋挞，明明葡式，吃完却让你产生一种本地户口的归属感。

Crocs are what happens when a garden clog wins a radio contest and thinks it’s fashion. They’ve got more holes than the excuse you gave for wearing them in public. Those little Jibbitz charms don’t make them “expressive”; they make your feet look like a refrigerator door covered in magnets. Crocs somehow manage to be both waterproof and dignity-soluble. They squeak into a room like a toddler pushing a wet shopping cart, then have the nerve to be called “comfortable,” as if comfort is a legal defense. And Sport Mode? Please. Flipping that strap back doesn’t turn you into an athlete; it turns your ankles into witnesses. Crocs are the official shoe of “I gave up, but I’m still running errands.”
Crocs最神奇的是，它明明是一双鞋，却长得像一块被老鼠开过会的橡皮。鞋面全是洞，说是透气，其实是给小石子办VIP通道。下雨天穿它，你脚趾能第一时间知道哪个水坑水温合适。还有那个后跟带，放前面叫拖鞋，拨后面叫“运动模式”，仿佛把安全带系在泡沫箱上就能上高速。最狠的是还要往洞里插小饰品：你以为在装可爱，其实是在给鞋的毛孔贴冰箱贴。

UGG boots look like someone taught a loaf of bread to give up. They’re the only footwear that says, “I want my feet to be warm, but my standards to be at room temperature.” That sheepskin lining is cozy, sure—if your goal is to walk around with two emotional support lambs strapped to your ankles. And the moment it rains? Congratulations, your $180 beige pillows have evolved into sad, lumpy sponges. UGGs don’t have soles so much as a vague suggestion of resistance between you and the pavement. They collapse inward after three wears like they just heard some bad news. UGG boots: for people who looked at slippers and thought, “Can I make these less elegant and more expensive?”
UGG雪地靴最神奇的是，它叫“雪地靴”，但你真踩雪里，回来就像两块浸过酱油的发糕。外面麂皮吸水，里面羊毛捂脚，走十分钟脚开始自带桑拿；再一脱，袜子像刚从小火锅里捞出来。它还没有鞋型，穿久了脚后跟直接踩塌，远看像两只被生活压扁的骆驼蹄。最离谱是这么贵，买的不是鞋，是冬天的尊严：我冷可以，但我的脚必须看起来很会过圣诞。

Las Vegas is the only city on Earth that looks like a billionaire’s fever dream but smells like cheap cigars and poor decisions. It’s a cultural melting pot, if that pot was filled with twenty-four-dollar margaritas, pawn shop receipts, and middle-aged men wearing Oakleys indoors. Where else can you lose your kid’s college fund by pushing a button, walk out of a fake pyramid, and get slapped in the face by a guy handing out trading cards for escorts? Vegas loves to brag, "What happens here, stays here." Yeah, mainly because you had to sell your return flight ticket to double down on a soft sixteen. The whole town is engineered to make you forget the time, which is easy when every ceiling is a painted sky and they’re pumping pure oxygen at the penny slots just to keep Grandma conscious.

拉斯维加斯是个极其荒谬的地方。你刚下飞机，连行李都没拿到，登机口旁边就立着一排老虎机。它简直是在对你说：“哥们，反正你的钱最后都要留在这儿，不如咱们把中间去酒店的打车费给省了？”

这地方到底有多假？他们在最缺水的沙漠正中间，塞满了山寨的埃菲尔铁塔和自由女神像。你在威尼斯人酒店坐着室内假运河的贡多拉，听墨西哥大叔用散装意大利语给你唱情歌，头顶是画在天花板上、永远不会天黑的假蓝天。

最讽刺的是，在这个毫无底线、连呼吸的空气都是人造冷气的城市里，唯一的“真实”，居然是你刚在楼下轮盘赌上，真金白银地输光了下半辈子的房贷。

Jackfruit, looking at you is like looking at a dinosaur egg that went through a goth phase. You’re covered in spikes and weigh forty pounds. Carrying you home from the grocery store isn't shopping; it's a CrossFit workout. 

And cutting into you? Absolute nightmare. You bleed industrial-grade superglue. People have to lube up their knives with cooking oil just to butcher you. Who wants a snack that requires foreplay with a bottle of Crisco? 

Then there’s your identity crisis. You're a fruit, but vegans keep trying to gaslight us into believing you're pulled pork. Newsflash: drowning a giant, stringy booger in Sweet Baby Ray’s doesn't make it a pig. You don't taste like meat; you taste like a Juicy Fruit wrapper that gave up on its dreams. Stop trying to be dinner, you spiky imposter.

吃菠萝蜜根本不是吃水果，而是一场大型外科手术。你见过开哪种水果，还得先给菜刀抹上一层食用油做润滑的吗？切开之后，里面全是白色的天然树脂黏液，弄到手上三天洗不掉，跟强力胶似的。然后你得戴着手套，在一堆密密麻麻的黄色“破布条”里，费劲巴拉地往外抠果肉。

买个三十斤的菠萝蜜，光外壳和那堆拔不完的破丝儿就占了二十七斤。你在案板前站了俩小时，出了一身汗，终于抠出来一小盘黄色肉包。满心欢喜咬上一口，好家伙，里面居然还藏着个板栗那么大的核！这哪是吃水果，这就是在废墟里搞生还者搜救啊！

Let's talk about durian. The only fruit that requires a biohazard suit and a safe word to open. People call it the "King of Fruits." Yeah, if the kingdom is a humid dumpster. Who was the first guy to find a medieval spiked mace smelling like hot gym socks and rotting onions, and think, "I bet the mushy yellow alien brains inside taste delicious"?

You know you’re a terrible snack when you’re legally banned from public transit. You can bring a live chicken on a train in Singapore, but a durian triggers a hostage negotiation. And durian lovers act so superior about it. "Oh, you just have to get past the initial aroma of a ruptured gas leak." No, I don't, Kevin. I'll just eat an apple like someone who doesn't actively hate their own mouth.

我一直觉得榴莲是自然界最充满敌意的防御系统。外壳长满尖刺，散发着煤气泄漏的恶臭，大自然分明把“别碰老子”刻在了它的基因里！结果人类不仅非要吃，它还卖得死贵！

你花两百块买个流星锤回家，冒着工伤的风险撬开，就为了掏出几坨黄色的软泥。最离谱的是买它还带赌博性质，俗称“开榴莲盲盒”，运气不好开出来的全是厚皮和巨大的核。

花了巨款，你吃的时候还得像做贼一样。高铁酒店都不让进，在家吃完还得连夜下楼丢果壳，生怕邻居报警说你家在炖屎。花大价钱买个带刺的生化武器，体验一种卑微的犯罪感，这哪里是吃水果，这就是斯德哥尔摩综合征吧！

Macau is what happens when Portugal gets drunk, sleeps with a slot machine, and leaves the baby for China to raise. You call yourselves the "Vegas of Asia," but let’s be real. Vegas has Cirque du Soleil; Macau has chain-smoking mainland uncles aggressively slapping baccarat tables at 9 AM. It’s not a vacation spot, it’s a giant ATM where tourists lose their life savings before crying at a pawn shop on the Avenida de Almeida Ribeiro. You’re so desperate for space you dumped dirt in the ocean to build the Cotai Strip—a place that somehow looks like Venice, Paris, and a dystopian duty-free mall simultaneously. But hey, at least you have egg tarts. That totally makes up for being Hong Kong's boring, gambling-addicted little brother.

去澳门你会发现，这城市的公共交通全靠赌场互相抢客。大家都去蹭“发财车”，但这名字太讽刺了，坐上去以为去发财，出来时连买水的钱都没了。

好在赌场里依云免费拿，奶茶免费喝！就是有点贵，你往赌桌上一坐，这杯免费奶茶成本得两万五。

最绝的是结账，你递港币，老板理直气壮找你一把澳门葡币。这玩意一过拱北口岸就成了纪念品，拿它去珠海买东西，老板看你的眼神仿佛你刚从大富翁里抢了银行。最后你站在大三巴跟前，攥着一把花不出去的葡币，感觉自己和那面牌坊一样，彻底被掏空了。

Let’s talk about UGG boots. The only footwear that makes human feet look like two freshly baked loaves of sourdough. I don’t know who decided we needed a shoe that provides the warmth of a blast furnace with the structural integrity of a damp paper towel, but here we are. You wear them for two months, the heel completely collapses, and suddenly you’re walking on the side of your own ankle like a newborn calf. They're made of sheepskin, which is ironic, because wearing them proves you just follow the flock straight to the Target checkout line. And God forbid it actually rains in these so-called winter boots. One puddle and they instantly turn into soggy, salt-stained sponges that smell like a wet golden retriever. Two hundred dollars just to get swamp foot by Thanksgiving.

Crocs are the only footwear that come pre-perforated so your dignity can escape faster. They look like they were 3D-printed by a toddler who hates fashion and loves Swiss cheese. And don't get me started on Jibbitz. You're literally plugging rubber holes with tiny plastic Shreks like you're bedazzling a kitchen colander. 

Then there’s the heel strap. People actually call flipping it back "sports mode." What sport are you playing in foam clogs? Competitive gardening? Speed-shuffling away from a date who just realized what's on your feet? Flipping that strap doesn't make you an athlete, it just secures the wearable Tupperware to your ankle so it doesn't fly off while your sweaty soles squeak like a plunger fighting a wet walrus. You're not a track star, Kevin, you're a tired line cook on a smoke break.

大家好，我是那种在水果店看到榴莲会绕道走的人。不是因为它臭，是因为这玩意儿太装了。别的香蕉苹果烂了就是烂了，榴莲不，它管那叫“熟成”。你花两百块请回家一个果王，它在你家厨房散发出的味道，怎么说呢，就像你把健身包忘在三伏天的后备箱里，过了个周末还往里面倒了罐炼乳。打开它更像拆弹，戴手套拿刀比划半天，最后挖出来那点金黄的肉，质地介于奶油和烂洋葱之间。最气人的是吃完打嗝，一股子汽油味混着糖精往上翻。我朋友还安慰我：“这才是高级香。”我说算了吧，我宁愿在家供个榴莲模型，至少不会半夜在垃圾桶里对我进行化学攻击。

洞洞鞋最离谱的是它的商业模式。你买了一双全是窟窿的橡胶海绵，然后他们告诉你：“嘿，你得花钱买‘鞋花’把洞堵上哦！”这简直是鞋界DLC，买鞋两百，配齐上面的汉堡和小熊得花八百，走在街上像是一脚踩进娃娃机里拔不出来了。

更好笑的是它居然还有“运动模式”。把后跟那根塑料带往下一拉，你就运动了？你穿它唯一能跑起来的原因，是下雨天鞋洞里灌满水，脚在里面疯狂打滑，为了不劈叉只能连滚带爬。一整个夏天穿下来，脱下鞋脚背上全是波点晒痕，去医院大夫看了都得怀疑你是不是变异成了七星瓢虫。

Jackfruit, you are the world’s most overqualified paperweight. You look like a medieval weapon crossed with a tumor, and you leak latex like a broken glue factory the second someone tries to cut you. Your one party trick is being vegan pulled pork, which means your entire personality is pretending to be something actually delicious. Even your smell can’t commit: ripe jackfruit reeks like bubblegum left in a dumpster, half tropical candy, half onion regret. Inside, you’re just a thousand stringy bulbs of wet cardboard hiding boulder-sized seeds, each one coated in slime that could anchor a ship. You take two hours to break down, ruin every knife you own, and at the end you have a fruit that tastes like a Capri Sun that gave up. You’re not food; you’re a hostage situation with fiber.

You’re a Las Vegas that got colonized by a pastry chef. Your entire GDP is one Chinese tourist angrily losing his kid’s tuition at a baccarat table while eating a pork chop bun. You built a fake Eiffel Tower, fake Venetian canals, and a fake London bus—because the only authentic thing about you is the crushing existential despair of a croupier on a Tuesday. Your biggest historical landmark is a wall that fell down. The Ruins of St. Paul’s is just a façade with commitment issues, much like your cultural identity: Portuguese enough for egg tarts, Chinese enough for the loan sharks to find you. You’re so small that your “skyline” is basically four ATM machines wearing sequins. And still, every cab driver will take the long way through Cotai just to watch you pray.

Las Vegas: where you pay $400 a night for a room with a carpet that’s absorbed more regret than a confessional, and the only thing older than the clientele is the smell of stale cigarette smoke woven into the curtains. This city took a perfectly good desert and said, “Let’s add fountains that cost more than the water rights of three states, then make you walk past six guys flicking escort cards at your crotch just to see them.” You can get married by an Elvis who lost his jumpsuit to a pawn shop, gamble away your kid’s college fund on a slot machine that hasn’t paid out since O.J. was acquitted, and then celebrate with a $19.99 buffet where the shrimp have seen more freezer burn than a corpse in a mob documentary. The only thing authentic about the “Paris” casino is the regret when you realize you flew across the country to stand under a fake Eiffel Tower eating a hot dog that costs more than your flight. Vegas isn’t a city, it’s a debt collection agency with a roller coaster and a zip line.
澳门这地方，赌场的冷气开得比北极还足，进去转一圈出来，我都不知道自己输的是钱还是体温。最离谱的是那些免费穿梭巴士，明明就隔一条街，它非要带你绕澳门半岛三圈，让你深刻体会什么叫“来都来了”。还有那个大三巴，全世界游客挤在一堵墙前面拍照，我寻思这墙要真能带来好运，澳门人早把它镶金边供起来了，还能让你们随便摸？

Crocs: proof that you can leave the house in a colander with a seatbelt on it. They look like orthopedic gardening clogs designed by a toddler who was told to draw a boat and gave up. You can't even say they're for comfort—wearing these is like hugging a pool noodle with foot fungus. And the little holes? Ah yes, so your dignity can leak out. You paid fifty bucks to look like SpongeBob’s weird aunt at a water park. You put charms on them like that helps—congrats, you accessorized a biohazard. “But they’re practical!” So is a hazmat suit, Brenda, but you don’t wear it to brunch. The only thing Crocs are versatile with is ruining every outfit, every occasion, and every first date you’ve ever been on. They don’t even stay on your feet; they just flap around like two rubber ducks fleeing a crime scene.

Durian, you are what happens when a coconut joins a biker gang and dies in a gas leak. You don’t smell “distinctive”—you smell like a landfill’s armpit after a durian-eating contest, which is just you all the way down. Hotels across Southeast Asia have signs with your spiky silhouette crossed out, not because of your looks, but because one open husk can evacuate a lobby faster than a fire alarm. Inside, your flesh is warm custard that was stored in a gym bag with raw shallots and turpentine. People call you the “king of fruits,” but that’s just a polite way of saying nobody with functioning nostrils would sit next to you on a bus. Your aftertaste is a garlic-onion burp that punches you every time you speak for six hours. Even your own defense mechanism is a falling spiked skull. People eat you only to prove they can.

UGG雪地靴，我称它为“薛定谔的鞋”。买之前你看广告：超模穿，明星穿，光腿穿，感觉这鞋自带拉腿功能。买回来自己穿，哎，这什么？我脚踝呢？我脚踝是不是离家出走了？它就是一双把脚踝吃掉的鞋，穿上之后你小腿直接从地面长出来，像两根会走路的法棍面包。

而且它根本没有“鞋型”这个概念。穿仨月之后，它开始照着你的脚形自己长，而且只学坏不学好。最后它长得比你亲妈都了解你的脚，拇外翻都给你复刻出来。它不是鞋，它是你脚的档案管理员。

UGG boots look like two bloated marshmallows that got into a fight with a sheep and lost. You’re not footwear; you’re a cry for help wrapped in shearling. That shapeless, ankle-swallowing silhouette makes every leg look like a traffic cone dipped in oatmeal. And the name? “UGG” isn’t a brand, it’s the sound your feet make when they realize they’re trapped in a sweat lodge of their own making. You’ve got the structural integrity of a deflated whoopee cushion and the color palette of a nicotine-stained cloud. People don’t walk in you; they waddle, like penguins who’ve given up on dignity. You’re the only shoe that gets uglier the more you’re worn, yet somehow people still pay $200 to look like they’re commuting in a pair of microwaved slippers. Congratulations, UGGs: you’ve turned “basic” into a foot condition.

我一直没搞懂UGG雪地靴，它明明叫“雪地靴”，但它最大的天敌居然是雪。你冬天出门看到下雪，第一反应绝不是“太好了我有雪地靴”，而是“完蛋了！我的翻毛皮要留水印了！”这就好像你花重金雇了个保镖，一遇到劫匪保镖赶紧躲到你身后说：“哥你挡着我点，我晕血。”

而且穿上它，你的脚踝就彻底消失了，整个人就像两根筷子插在两个大烤面包上。最绝的是它穿久了后跟必定往外塌，你在街上看到前面有人呈外八字疯狂拖着脚、看起来像两个脚踝同时骨折了一样——别报警，她没出车祸，她只是穿了一双三年的UGG。

我上次买了个菠萝蜜，五十块钱，扛回家像扛了颗地雷。一刀下去，它先给我喷了一手白色胶水，那玩意儿比502还顽固，洗洁精洗不掉，最后我拿食用油搓了十分钟，手滑得连门把手都拧不开。好不容易切开，里面果肉一颗颗窝在黏糊糊的筋膜里，像一群外星虫卵等着孵化。吃一颗果肉，吐一颗核，核比鹌鹑蛋还大，我算了一下，五十块钱里三十五块买的是核。味道呢，齁甜，像菠萝和香蕉搞暧昧没搞成，急眼了撒了一袋糖精。最绝的是吃完，手指头缝里那股黏胶味三天不散，玩手机屏幕都粘指纹。我劝大家，菠萝蜜这东西，买之前先问问自己：你是想吃水果，还是想给水果打工俩小时？
榴莲这东西，就是水果界的路怒症。外面一身狼牙棒，里面几块软趴趴的黄瓤，你花钱买它，还得先被它扎手。切开那一刻，整间屋子像有人在暖气旁忘了洗的袜子，邻居以为我家下水道成了精。最离谱的是大家还夸它：“闻着臭，吃着香。”这不叫夸，这叫它先骗过你的鼻子，再骗你的钱包。果肉还藏在刺壳里，剥出来像开盲盒，开到小的那房，老板说这是“报恩榴莲”。我谢谢它，它报恩的方式，是让我花两百块吃一口臭烘烘的奶油。

Durian is the only fruit that behaves like a biological weapon with a PR budget. It’s a spiky medieval mace filled with custard that learned to hold a grudge. People say it smells like heaven and hell had a custody battle; more like a gym sock marinated in crème brûlée inside a hot dumpster. You have to fight through armor just to be disappointed by an onion-flavored cheesecake. It’s illegal in hotels not because it’s dangerous, but because housekeeping deserves hazard pay. Durian fans don’t enjoy it; they endure it, then smirk at everyone else like suffering is a membership card.

Crocs洞洞鞋，我一直觉得是设计师跟脚趾有仇。鞋面上打那么多洞，说是透气，其实穿它走一趟石子路，回家能从鞋里倒出半条绿化带。那些洞对你唯一的用处，就是逼你再花钱买Jibbitz把它堵上——你花三百买双鞋，再花两百把洞填满，最后得到一双更丑的普通拖鞋。还有后面那根带子，放下来叫“运动模式”，好像它真能运动。我试过跑两步，鞋先到终点，我脚上只剩两个洞的印子。最绝的是它那个材质，轻得离谱，穿上像没穿，但颜色又亮得站在月球上都能看见你。穿Crocs的感觉就是：你的脚在坐牢，但牢房是镂空的。

Jackfruit, you’re the fruit equivalent of a group project: massive, sticky, and everyone pretends you’re easier to handle than you are. You smell like a banana went to a nail salon and got into a fistfight with a pineapple. People call you “vegan pulled pork,” which is just a compliment to pork and an insult to sandwiches. You have a hundred seeds, all covered in slime, guarded by latex so aggressive it should be classified as a restraining order. You weigh as much as a toddler and cost more than therapy, yet you still require forty minutes of oiling up just to touch. You’re not versatile; you’re commitment. Even your name sounds like a guy named Jack claiming credit for a fruit.
拉斯维加斯机场的行李转盘旁边就摆着老虎机——你人还没落地，它已经先帮你把回程机票钱输了。赌场里没有钟，没有窗户，我在里面输到觉得才晚上十点，出来一看，太阳照着假的自由女神像，已经第二天中午了。最绝的是那头还有 drive-thru 婚礼，你在车里说“我愿意”，窗口递出来的不是戒指，是离婚表格，让你顺手签。拉斯维加斯整个城市就一句话：太阳是真的，自由女神是假的，只有你输掉的钱和刚结的婚是真的。

Las Vegas is the only city built so adults can lose a mortgage payment at blackjack while pretending it’s self-care. It markets itself as “what happens here stays here,” which is brave for a place where everyone posts their buffet plate and fake Eiffel Tower selfie within four minutes. The Strip is a desert strip mall with delusions of grandeur: Venice in a gondola, Egypt in a pyramid, New York in a coaster, and dignity nowhere in the gift shop. Locals call it Sin City, but mostly it smells like carpet cleaner, desperation, and Celine Dion’s final note. Even the Bellagio fountains have more choreography than the tourists stumbling toward a 2 a.m. shrimp cocktail.
菠萝蜜这水果特别像一种考验。你买回家，它不像吃的，像个长刺的瑜伽球。切它得像拆炸弹，刀进去先被胶住，拔出来能拉丝，手粘得比你前任还紧。剥半天，终于露出一格格黄肉，像蒜瓣发了财，每瓣还揣个核。你以为吃的是果肉，它还附赠一盘要水煮的核。吃完一称，皮比人重，核比肉多，手上三天还有味。它不是水果，它是热带派来的手工课。

Macau, you’re Las Vegas if it got shrunk in the wash and left in a Portuguese bakery. Your entire personality is a casino lobby pretending to be a UNESCO site. Tourists take one photo at Senado Square, eat an egg tart, and then lose rent money under lights designed to make midnight feel like a tax audit. The Cotai Strip is basically a slot-machine airport with better fountains and worse decisions. You built a tower so people can bungee off it, which says your main export is regret with a view. Even your typhoon signals are more dramatic than your nightlife: T8 means stay inside, T10 means the casinos finally feel airy. You’re not a city; you’re a VIP junket wearing azulejo tiles.

Crocs are what happens when a garden hose files for personhood. They look like rubber clogs designed by an orthopedic surgeon who hated feet and color. The holes aren’t ventilation; they’re pre-drilled escape routes for your dignity. Jibbitz are just tiny plastic participation trophies clipped onto shoes that already surrendered to fashion. Wearing Crocs says, “I need traction, cushioning, and the option to be hospitalized.” They’re comfortable like a foam mattress in a studio apartment: you sink in slowly while everyone watches. Even the strap is a lie—part emergency brake, part “I’m trying to make this work.” Crocs aren’t footwear; they’re amphibious slippers for people who think “sporty” means the walk from couch to fridge.
拉斯维加斯这地方，整个城市就一个设计理念：别让你找到出口。机场一下飞机就是老虎机，仿佛行李转盘是诱惑你赌博的前菜。酒店大堂永远没有钟，走廊永远绕回赌场，你想去电梯？先穿过三百台老虎机，连想回房间都得先输两把。最离谱的是窗外，你花两百刀订了景观房，拉开窗帘，对面是假的埃菲尔铁塔、假的金字塔，旁边还站着个抽假烟的自由女神。沙漠里硬挖运河，商场里下人造雨，好像自然欠他们钱。这里唯一真诚的东西，是账单。

Durian is a fruit that inspires strong opinions, and it has both commendable qualities and notable drawbacks. On the positive side, its flesh offers a rich, custard-like texture and a complex, subtly sweet flavor that many describe as nutty and savory. It is also a good source of energy, dietary fiber, and several vitamins and minerals. However, its powerful odor is a significant barrier for some, as it lingers on the breath and in enclosed spaces. The fruit is also calorie-dense and high in natural sugars, which may not suit every diet. Additionally, its heavy, spiny husk makes preparation somewhat difficult. Overall, durian is best appreciated in moderation by those who enjoy its intensity.

榴莲是一种特点极为鲜明的热带水果。它的优点在于果肉质地绵密细腻，入口有类似奶油的顺滑感，甜度较高，风味浓郁且富有层次，喜欢的人往往会被这种独特的香气和口感深深吸引。从营养角度看，榴莲含有丰富的碳水化合物、维生素C、钾元素和膳食纤维，能为身体快速补充能量。

不足之处也同样明显。它气味强烈，对不习惯的人来说可能难以接受，甚至在公共场合食用会影响到他人。此外，榴莲热量和糖分都偏高，过量食用容易增加身体负担，不适合需要控制血糖或体重的人群。它的价格通常也高于一般水果，果壳带刺，剥取时需要留意安全。总体而言，榴莲适合欣赏其风味且身体状况允许的人适量品尝。

菠萝蜜是一种具有独特风味的热带水果，在口感与营养价值上都有较突出的表现。其果肉厚实，味道香甜，带有柔和的果香，熟度适中时口感细腻而有嚼劲。它富含膳食纤维、维生素C和多种矿物质，对促进消化和补充能量有一定帮助。同时，菠萝蜜的果肉可鲜食，种子煮熟后也可食用，利用率较高，是比较经济实惠的热带水果。

不过，菠萝蜜也存在一些需要注意的地方。例如，其含糖量较高，不宜一次食用过多，尤其是需要控制血糖的人群应适量食用。切开时果胶黏性较强，处理起来稍有不便；此外，果实体积较大，家庭食用可能需要分批保存。整体而言，菠萝蜜风味独特、营养丰富，只要适量食用，仍是值得推荐的水果之一。

Jackfruit offers notable versatility, particularly as a plant-based meat alternative due to its fibrous, pull-apart texture and mild ability to absorb seasonings. It is also a good source of dietary fiber, vitamin C, and potassium, and the tree’s high yield makes it an efficient crop. However, fresh jackfruit can be difficult to handle: its large size, sticky latex sap, and tough rind require time and effort to prepare. Ripe fruit has a very sweet, pungent aroma that not everyone enjoys, while canned young jackfruit in brine may be bland without careful seasoning and can contain added sodium. Those with latex allergies should also exercise caution. Overall, it is a useful ingredient whose benefits are balanced by practical drawbacks.

UGG boots are what happens when sheepskin wins a participation trophy. They’re shaped like a toddler’s drawing of a foot, with all the structure of a wet napkin stuffed in a couch. You pay luxury prices to look like your ankles have been swallowed by two depressed pillows. The outside says “I bought these at a mall,” while the inside says “I haven’t washed them since the Obama administration.” They’re the only footwear that makes a 40-degree day feel like a personal failing. And when the heel collapses into that crusty, folded-over slouch, it’s not fashion—it’s a boot surrendering to gravity, sweat, and regret.

Las Vegas offers a wide range of entertainment, dining, and lodging options that can suit many budgets and preferences. The concentration of shows, casinos, and restaurants makes it easy for visitors to find activities without traveling far. Many hotels are well maintained, and service staff are generally professional and attentive.

At the same time, the city can feel overwhelming. Noise, crowds, and bright lighting are constant in the main resort areas, which may be tiring for those seeking a quieter trip. Smoking is permitted in many casinos, and the scent can be noticeable indoors. Costs for food, drinks, and transportation on the Strip are often higher than in other destinations. The city also relies heavily on gambling and nightlife, so visitors who do not enjoy those activities may find fewer appealing options after a day or two.

Overall, Las Vegas is best suited to those who appreciate high-energy urban entertainment and are comfortable with its particular atmosphere.

Macau offers a distinctive blend of Portuguese and Chinese heritage, which is evident in its architecture, cuisine, and cultural traditions. The historic centre is well preserved, and sites such as the Ruins of St. Paul’s are both interesting and accessible. The city is generally safe, and public transport is efficient for its size.

At the same time, the heavy focus on the casino industry shapes much of the atmosphere, which may not appeal to visitors seeking a quieter or more culturally immersive experience. Outside the main heritage areas, parts of the city can feel crowded and commercial. Dining and accommodation can also be expensive compared with nearby destinations. Overall, Macau is worth visiting for its history and unique character, though it is best appreciated with realistic expectations about its modern, tourism-driven side.
拉斯维加斯是一座特色鲜明的娱乐与度假城市。优点方面，这里集中了大量高品质酒店、餐厅和购物场所，各类演出与娱乐项目丰富，服务水平普遍专业高效，对游客来说交通和配套也较为便利。不足方面，城市整体以博彩和夜生活为核心，商业气息较浓，环境相对喧闹，可能不太适合偏好安静或带低龄儿童出行的游客。此外，夏季气候炎热干燥，日常消费和度假成本也偏高。总体而言，它适合短途体验，但不宜期待宁静或较深的文化氛围。

澳门是一座兼具中西文化特色的城市，整体城市风貌独特，历史城区保存较为完整，街道整洁，公共设施完善，旅游服务也相对成熟。对于游客来说，交通接驳方便，景点集中，适合短途游览。饮食方面选择丰富，既有地道的粤式风味，也有葡国菜等多元餐饮。

不足之处在于城市面积有限，旺季时热门景点和娱乐场所人流密集，部分区域较为拥挤。此外，经济结构较为单一，对旅游和博彩业依赖较高，本地居民的生活空间与游客活动区域有时重叠，可能带来一定不便。总体而言，澳门有其独特魅力，也存在发展中的局限。
我朋友穿Crocs，说自己很松弛。我说你这不叫松弛，叫给脚开了个开放式办公区。十几个洞，脚趾随时探头问：到站了吗？下雨更绝，外面下大雨，鞋里养小鱼，走一步咕叽一声，像踩死一块会道歉的海绵。最离谱是鞋花，一双塑料洞洞鞋还要插满小配饰，远看像拖鞋界戴满发卡的教导主任。你别说它丑，人家说这是舒适。对，舒适得像把脚直接塞进外卖保温袋，还顺手给你按了几个通风口。

Crocs洞洞鞋在 casual 鞋履中具有辨识度，优点与不足都比较明确。  
优点是轻便、透气，EVA材质让鞋子整体很轻，鞋面孔洞设计利于排汗和快干，夏季或潮湿环境穿脱方便，也容易冲洗。鞋底缓冲感适中，短时间站立或行走有一定舒适度，鞋型宽松，对脚背高或脚宽的人比较友好。  
不足之处在于支撑性和包裹感一般，长时间行走或快走时，后跟与足弓缺乏足够固定，可能增加疲劳感。鞋底在湿滑瓷砖或油污地面防滑表现不稳定。另外，外观风格比较休闲，搭配场景相对受限，正式或商务场合不太合适。  
整体来看，它更适合居家、沙滩、短途散步或雨天替代鞋，不适合作为长时间步行的主力鞋。
UGG雪地靴最离谱的是，它叫雪地靴，但真下雪你穿它出门，就像给脚套了两只羊腿。里面毛厚到脚一伸进去就失联，走路全靠脚趾在羊毛里摸索方向。远看像踩了两个发酵面团，近看还是羊皮毛一体。雪一化，水顺着毛往里渗，它不防水，只负责把冷和潮一起保温。进门一脱，热气混着羊毛味往上冒，室友问我是不是把羊炖在脚上了。更绝的是后跟，穿两周就塌，UGG自动从雪地靴降级成羊毛拖鞋，花一千多买个随时能回家的借口。

You know what tropical fruits are? Nature’s way of saying, “I made apples and oranges too easy for you.” These things are the trust-fund kids of the produce aisle—all flash, no convenience. They demand a machete, a geometry degree, and an apology before you can even taste them. And what do you get? A mouthful of sugar water that goes bad if you look at it wrong.

They smell like a candle store exploded, but half of them taste like wet cardboard wearing perfume. You ever bite into one and it’s just… slime with ambition? Seeds the size of your thumb, fibers that floss your teeth against your will, and skins so thick you need a safety briefing. They’re not food—they’re a hostage negotiation. You paid eight dollars for one piece of fruit, and it still judges you for not knowing its “peak ripeness window” is seventeen minutes long. Meanwhile, a banana—oh wait, I can’t name names. Just trust me, one of you is fine. The rest belong in a smoothie, where your sins can be hidden.

澳门最神奇的地方，是它明明很小，却能让你三天走不出赌场。你在拱北排队两小时，进去后发现澳门只够你发个定位；导航说前方到达目的地，我还没来得及系好安全带。大三巴人多得像早高峰，走近一看，就一面墙，旁边卖蛋挞的阿姨比古迹还烫手。金光大道更离谱，威尼斯人给你假天空，巴黎人给你假铁塔，伦敦人给你假大本钟，一天环游欧洲，护照不用盖章，钱包得先开光。发财车免费坐，坐上去像被财神绑架：不赌两把，都对不起这空调。澳门最像主题乐园：门票不要钱，出口全在老虎机后面。

UGG雪地靴的主要优点是保暖性能出色，内里通常采用羊毛材质，穿着柔软舒适，在寒冷干燥的环境下能有效保持双脚温暖。经典款式设计简洁，搭配休闲装较为方便，部分鞋底也具备一定的防滑效果。

不足之处在于鞋面多为翻毛皮材质，防水和抗污能力较弱，遇水后容易留下痕迹，日常清洁和保养需要花费较多精力。此外，鞋型相对宽松，对足弓的支撑性一般，长时间行走可能会感到支撑不足。价格方面也偏高，整体更适合在干冷天气短时间穿着，而非作为全天候或雨雪天气的鞋款。

Crocs offer several practical strengths. They are lightweight, easy to clean, quick-drying, and reasonably cushioned for short-term wear. The ventilation holes improve airflow and make them convenient in wet or messy environments, and the adjustable heel strap adds a useful fit option.

However, there are notable weaknesses. The wide, bulky silhouette can look out of place in more formal or professional settings. The same ventilation holes allow small stones and debris to enter, and arch support is limited, which may lead to discomfort during extended walking or standing. The synthetic material can also trap heat and moisture, resulting in perspiration and odor over time.

Overall, Crocs are a sensible choice for casual, low-impact, or water-related use, but they are less appropriate for prolonged wear or dressier occasions.

UGG boots offer notable warmth and comfort, thanks to their soft sheepskin lining and plush interior. They are easy to slip on and provide reliable insulation in cold, dry weather. The simple design also pairs well with casual outfits, which contributes to their lasting popularity. However, there are some practical drawbacks. The suede exterior is vulnerable to moisture, stains, and salt, so the boots require regular waterproofing and careful upkeep. They also lack strong arch support, making them less suitable for extended walking or all-day wear. In wet or icy conditions, traction can be limited. Overall, UGG boots are a comfortable choice for mild winter days and indoor coziness, but they are not the most durable or supportive option for harsher weather or heavy use.

朋友们，你们有没有发现，热带水果这种东西，根本就是水果界的戏精。

它们长得那叫一个用力过猛啊，浑身是刺，头顶长叶子，外壳硬得能砸核桃。你买回家往桌上一放，不知道的以为我请了个菠萝形状的门神回来镇宅。

每次想开一个热带水果，我都觉得我不是在吃水果，是在拆某种古老文明的封印。切开之前，你永远不知道里面是惊喜还是惊吓，有的里面甜得要命，有的里面酸得我眉毛当场离家出走，有的里面那个口感……我说不上来，像是在嚼一块被太阳晒了三天的海绵。

最关键的是，这些水果还特别会PUA你。你在超市看它其貌不扬，买回来放两天，忽然整个厨房开始弥漫一种非常霸道的味道，闻着吧，像香水洒了，又像什么东西坏了。你也不确定，但就那个味儿，它能告诉全楼的人：这家，买了热带水果。

我朋友说热带水果能提升幸福感，我说是啊，切开、吃完、清理完，它还活着没吃完的部分在冰箱里继续散发魅力，这幸福感，太持久了。

你们发现没有，赌城这地方特别有仪式感。进门先给你发张卡，往里头充钱，感觉跟去食堂打饭似的。更绝的是没有窗户！也没有钟！这帮人太懂心理学了——让你分不清白天黑夜，输到怀疑人生的时候一看表，好家伙，凌晨四点半，你还以为刚吃完午饭。最搞笑的是里头那些老虎机，声音搞得跟过年似的，叮叮当当，不知道的以为谁家中了一百万。凑近一看，人家就赢了四块二，蹦得比中了彩票还欢。还有那些免费饮料，喝得你晕乎乎的。等清醒过来，钱包已经减肥成功了。

热带水果，就是水果界的戏精。外壳厚得跟防弹衣似的，切开之前像凶器，切开之后像事故现场。你花大几十买一个回家，先得上半小时解剖课，刀劈斧砍，最后得到一小碗果肉和一大袋建筑废料。味道更是霸道，不吃的人觉得你在炖袜子，吃的人管那叫大自然的香水。最气人的是熟没熟全凭缘分：买的时候硬得像石头，放两天直接烂成一滩情绪。你还不能把它当普通水果，它要求你伺候——切开要技术，保存要湿度，入口要勇气。最后你才明白，花大价钱买的不是水果，是参与感。

Casino cities are the only places on Earth where the local economy is built on the statistically proven fact that you, specifically, are bad at math. They’ve turned “almost won” into an industry. It’s the only city plan where the streets are designed like a labyrinth, the clocks are banned, and the oxygen is 40 percent carpet cleaner. You don’t visit a casino city; you’re absorbed by it. The main export is regret, and the main import is your retirement fund. The buffets are just a trough where they fatten you up before the slots finish the job. And the local culture? A few sad statues and a fake volcano. They built a whole city on the idea that the next pull of the lever will fix your life, but the only guaranteed jackpot is the one the city hits every time you park your car.

They’re all the same desperate theme park for adults who flunked math: a skyline of borrowed money, sidewalks sticky with spilled regret, and air that smells like stale cigarettes and shattered alimony. Casino cities are where architecture goes to die in neon, where every fountain is just a monument to someone else’s lost mortgage. The whole economy runs on tourists who confuse a buffet coupon for a personality and locals who think blackout curtains are a cultural landmark. There’s always a guy in a gold blazer who hasn’t seen sunlight since the Clinton administration, and a chapel where you can marry a mistake you met four drinks ago. These towns don’t have seasons; they have payout cycles. Their idea of fine dining is unlimited shrimp and a side of bankruptcy. Come for the jackpot, stay because you sold your return ticket at a pawnshop.

现在市面上的鞋，两极分化到像两个物种在打架。一类丑得惊心动魄，你穿上它走在街上，路人会以为你在用脚表演行为艺术。另一类贵得丧心病狂，你低头看一眼价格标签，脚趾头都能在鞋里抠出三室一厅。

最离谱的是设计逻辑——要么把鞋底做得比城墙还厚，踩上去像踩着两块砖头去赶集；要么薄得像张纸，走两步路你能清楚感受到地球的每一粒砂石跟你脚底板做的私聊。还有那种标榜“解构主义”的，一只鞋像被车碾过，另一只像半成品，两只拼一起就是一场灾难现场直播。

我就纳闷了，设计师是不是拿脚当试验田？要么丑到没人敢看，要么贵到没人敢买，中间地带直接蒸发。搞得我现在买鞋跟搞谍战似的，得先侦查半天，生怕一脚踩进时尚的陷阱里，既出不来钱，也出不来门。

我发现现在的鞋越来越极端了。要么薄得跟纸片似的，穿上感觉像光脚踩在盲道上，每一步都在给脚底做针灸；要么厚得跟踩高跷一样，出门一趟腿没累，心脏先恐高了。

中间值呢？没有。就像人类的审美也两极分化，要么瘦成闪电，要么胖成熊猫，你要是个正常体型，设计师觉得你不配穿鞋。

Divisive footwear brands are the only category of consumer goods where the purchase is also a personality test you didn’t consent to take. You’re not buying shoes; you’re enlisting in a cult, a meme, or a midlife crisis, depending on the sole.

One half of the population looks at these things and sees innovation. The other half sees a orthopedic mistake that escaped the lab. They’re ugly in a way that costs extra—like paying a ransom for your own dignity, but the kidnapper is a foam clog.

They promise comfort. What they deliver is an identity that screams, “I’ve given up, but I’ve given up in a limited-edition colorway.” People wear them to the airport, to weddings, to the brink of divorce. They’re not shoes. They’re a public admission that you’ve chosen convenience over ever being taken seriously again.

You know the type. The shoes that walk into a room five minutes before the person wearing them does. They cost more than your rent and look like a cyborg’s orthotic sneaker had a baby with a recycling bin. People don’t buy them for comfort or function; they buy them so other people will look down and start a fight. You can’t even call them ugly anymore, because the fans will tell you that’s the point. Congratulations, you paid four hundred dollars to look like you lost a bet with a storm drain.

And the cultish behavior? It’s a full-blown religion where the deity is a piece of molded foam. They’ll camp outside a store to buy a shoe that makes their foot look like a yam, then lecture you about "resale value." Bro, it’s footwear, not a 401(k). The only thing more inflated than the price is the ego of the guy explaining why they’re actually comfortable.
我一直觉得“赌城”这名字挺老实，它就是个城，但你进去之后，它把你当“城”管了。没有钟，没有窗，灯光永远像下午三点，让你觉得人生还早，其实外面你妈已经报警了。我进去时手机满电，出来时手机没电，人也快没电。服务员端着免费饮料，笑得比亲戚还亲，我以为是宾至如归，后来才明白是“宾至如归西”。最可怕的是出口，绕了半小时，最后从纪念品店后门钻出来，手里还多了个冰箱贴。我明明是去赢钱的，怎么变成去进货了？
